clue.text: The symbol of England at opening time?

definitions.text: The symbol of England at opening time?

parts.words: The symbol of England at opening time?
parts.note: England's emblem is the rose, and 'opening time' is not pub hours but the moment a flower begins to open

explanation.surface: A question about some national emblem being on show when the pubs open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening time' suggests British pub licensing hours; here it is the moment the rose, England's national flower, starts to open.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower bud is the unopened stage of the bloom, so the rose of England just before opening is this.

clue.text: Regions unite concerning charity

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for 'about' or 'concerning'
alms are gifts of charity to the poor

explanation.surface: Different regions coming together over charitable giving.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or domains, broad territories, so they are synonyms for regions.

clue.text: Luggage sent up to a place in Greece

indicators.note: in a down entry, something sent up is written from the bottom upwards, so the luggage word is turned round

parts.note: traps is an informal word for personal belongings or luggage

explanation.surface: Bags being shipped to a Greek destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was an ancient city-state of the Peloponnese, a famous place in Greece.

clue.text: Unlocked

parts.note: read not as 'with the lock open' but as 'without locks', the locks being locks of hair

explanation.surface: A single word that seems to describe an open door.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no hair on top has no locks of hair, so is in that sense un-locked.

clue.text: Financial obligation limited university entrance

indicators.note: the debt word limits, or bounds, the university letter by enclosing it

parts.note: a debt is money one is obliged to repay

explanation.surface: Student loans restricting who can get into university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like admission to a university but means a first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A first appearance on stage or in public is someone's entrance into that world.

clue.text: Give credit? You need faith to do it

definitions.meaning: to give credit to a story is to accept it as true

definitions.text: You need faith to do it
definitions.meaning: having faith is what this act requires; it is the act of holding something true

explanation.surface: A banker's remark that lending needs trust.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediting a claim means accepting it as true, and faith is trusting acceptance of truth; both senses are that verb.

clue.text: Skeleton service?

parts.note: a skeleton service is a minimal staff, but read literally it is a dinner service made of bone

explanation.surface: Seemingly a reference to a minimal staffing arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skeleton service' is a reduced service with minimal staff; the crockery made with bone ash makes it literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain made with bone ash is used for tea and dinner services, so it is literally a service of bone.

clue.text: Stagger up and get a dirty look

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the word is written bottom to top, so it is turned round

parts.note: to reel is to stagger or sway unsteadily

explanation.surface: A drunk lurching to their feet and getting a disapproving glare.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, lascivious or nasty sideways glance is a dirty look.

clue.text: I'd copies made of TV soaps, for example

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone recording copies of their favourite television dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective describing soaps: they come in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Television soap operas are told in successive instalments, so they are examples of serial, instalment-based drama.

clue.text: Taking someone on and winning

definitions.meaning: hiring or employing someone, or fighting them
charming or attractive, as in a winning smile

explanation.surface: Hiring someone and getting a victory out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The participle means both hiring or confronting someone and, as an adjective, charming and attractive.

clue.text: A number grow sick, get benefit

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
to ail is to be or become unwell

explanation.surface: Many people falling ill and claiming sickness pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of use or advantage is to benefit, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Bring round advance payment? Just joking!

indicators.note: the word Bring goes round the payment, enclosing it

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in advance, as in poker

explanation.surface: Asking for money up front, then saying it was only a jest.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-hearted teasing talk is joking, so someone doing it is just joking.

clue.text: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure

definitions.text: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure

parts.words: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure
parts.note: a striking thing is struck to light

explanation.surface: A remarkable echo of one of Lowry's painted people.
explanation.walkthrough: L S Lowry was an English painter of thin industrial figures, popularly called 'matchstick men'. 'Striking' means 'struck to make a flame'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stick struck to light a flame is struck, and resembles the thin stick figures Lowry painted.

clue.text: Wish to be extended

definitions.meaning: to yearn or wish for something
stretched out, lengthy in space or time

explanation.surface: Hoping something will be made bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for yearning and an adjective for something stretched great in length.

clue.text: It may be a tiny girl's reason for not singing

definitions.text: It may be a tiny girl's reason for not singing

parts.words: It may be a tiny girl's reason for not singing
parts.note: the girl sounds small, but a girl's voice-box inflammation would stop her singing; the hoarse voice is the 'tiny' one

explanation.surface: Why a little girl won't join in the song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiny' suggests a small child but points to a tiny, hoarse voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box causes hoarseness or loss of voice, a common reason a singer cannot perform.

clue.text: A conversion into a moist spray

definitions.text: A conversion into a moist spray

indicators.note: a conversion changes the form of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A process changing liquid into a fine damp mist.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while the letters of A and INTO A MOIST, with 'conversion' as signal, rearrange to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reducing a liquid to tiny droplets, as an aerosol does, is turning it into a fine mist.

clue.text: Lovers of the past

parts.note: not people fond of history, but former sweethearts

explanation.surface: People who are fond of history.
explanation.definitionFit: A former sweetheart is idiomatically a flame from before, a past romance still remembered.

clue.text: I'm engaged in property valuation

indicators.note: the I'm is engaged, or occupied, inside the property word

parts.note: an estate is a piece of landed property

explanation.surface: Someone working on assessing what a property is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: An approximate calculation of value is an estimate, as a builder gives before a job.

clue.text: Engaged men to incorporate new funds

indicators.note: the men take the new letter into their body, so it goes inside

parts.note: fiances are men engaged to be married

explanation.surface: Grooms-to-be pooling resources to set up a fresh fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Money resources, a person's or body's monetary affairs, are their funds.

clue.text: It's back to the accounts' book to write in "paid"

indicators.note: 'write in' says the writing word goes inside the run of letters
back means the word It's is read in reverse

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe
a diary is a book of accounts of daily events
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper entering a payment into the ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving a stipend or salary means being paid, as a stipendiary magistrate is.

clue.text: Lie, say, is found out without difficulty

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: An untruth discovered with no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without difficulty is doing it with ease.

clue.text: Confused tot given guidance

parts.note: to tot up is to add
led means guided

explanation.surface: A small child who is bewildered and is shown the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but is the verb meaning to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled or confused in thought, as an addled brain is.

clue.text: I'm a Muslim leader? Yes

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man confirming that he leads a Muslim congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, a cleric answering 'yes'; at the same time I'M + A + the leading letter of 'Muslim' builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader of prayers in a mosque, a Muslim religious leader, holds this title.

clue.text: Boycott warder, a scoundrel

parts.note: to black goods is to boycott them, a trade-union term
a guard is a warder

explanation.surface: Shunning a prison officer who has behaved badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boycott' looks like the name of the cricketer Geoffrey Boycott but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a dishonourable man, a rogue or villain, is a scoundrel.

clue.text: Thrash about the ring showing little craft

indicators.note: the thrashing word goes about, surrounding, the ring

parts.note: to cane is to beat or thrash
O is a ring shape

explanation.surface: A boxer flailing around the ring with little skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests skill but means a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small light boat paddled by hand is a little craft.

clue.text: Animal with fur and a round head

parts.note: a boa is a long fur or feather scarf

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A creature that is furry and has a round head.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild pig or uncastrated male pig is an animal.

clue.text: He always ends up in the relay race or tug of war

definitions.text: He always ends up in the relay race or tug of war

parts.words: He always ends up in the relay race or tug of war
parts.note: 'ends up' means is placed at the end: the last runner in a relay and the rear man on a tug-of-war rope

explanation.surface: A sportsman who keeps turning up in team events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends up' seems to mean 'finds himself in', but means 'takes the end position'.
explanation.definitionFit: The final runner of a relay team and the back man of a tug-of-war team both hold this title.

clue.text: It will get one off drill

indicators.note: off signals the one is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: the letters of the phrase it will; the run of letters after its first one is a coincidence of the deletion, not a hidden word, since 'one off' names the letter removed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Being excused military practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' looks like the military exercise but is the cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is a strong twilled cotton cloth, so this woven fabric is an example of it.

clue.text: Guarantees two points to new users

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: Assurances given to people trying a product for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Attempted to replant seed, say

indicators.note: replanting moves the seed letters elsewhere, so they are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: Trying to put seeds back in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to try or attempt it.
